body.en: In this lesson you will learn how to save LoRA and other PEFT adapters locally and on the Hugging Face Hub; distinguish a separate adapter from merged base-model weights; use merge_and_unload() to create a standalone fine-tuned model; and organize adapter checkpoints for production use.
body.fr: Dans cette leçon, vous apprendrez à enregistrer localement et sur le Hugging Face Hub des adaptateurs LoRA et autres PEFT, à distinguer un adaptateur séparé de poids fusionnés au modèle de base, à utiliser merge_and_unload() pour produire un modèle fine-tuné autonome et à organiser des checkpoints d’adaptateurs pour la production.

body.en:
## Objective

After training, decide deliberately which artifact to preserve. This lesson covers saving LoRA and other PEFT adapters locally or on the Hugging Face Hub, keeping an adapter separate from the base weights, creating a standalone fine-tuned model with `merge_and_unload()`, and organizing checkpoints for production use.

## Separate adapter or merged model?

A separate PEFT adapter stores the learned adaptation apart from the base model. It is usually the better artifact when several task-specific adapters share one base model, when you need to switch adapters, or when you want a compact artifact to version independently. Record the exact base-model revision, the adapter revision, the training data provenance, and evaluation context together; an adapter is not meaningful without its compatible base.

`merge_and_unload()` takes a loaded PEFT model and returns a standalone model with adapter weights merged into the base weights. It is not an in-place operation: assign its return value and use that returned model. Merging can remove the overhead of loading the adapter separately, but it trades away the convenience of swapping or unmerging that adapter in the merged artifact.

**Example.** A team maintains two adapters for the same base model: one for product support and one for internal knowledge retrieval. Keeping them separate permits one shared base model and independent releases. If the approved support version must run where only one model artifact is expected, the team can produce and version a merged release after recording the evidence that identifies it.

Official reference: [PEFT LoRA post-training documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/peft/en/package_reference/lora).
body.fr:
## Objectif

Après l’entraînement, choisissez délibérément l’artefact à conserver. Cette leçon traite de l’enregistrement local ou sur le Hugging Face Hub des adaptateurs LoRA et autres PEFT, de la distinction entre adaptateur séparé et poids de base fusionnés, de la création d’un modèle fine-tuné autonome avec `merge_and_unload()` et de l’organisation des checkpoints pour la production.

## Adaptateur séparé ou modèle fusionné ?

Un adaptateur PEFT séparé conserve l’adaptation apprise à part du modèle de base. C’est généralement le bon artefact lorsque plusieurs adaptateurs propres à une tâche partagent un même modèle de base, lorsque vous devez changer d’adaptateur ou lorsque vous voulez versionner indépendamment un artefact compact. Conservez avec lui la révision exacte du modèle de base, celle de l’adaptateur, la provenance des données d’entraînement et le contexte d’évaluation : un adaptateur n’a pas de sens sans sa base compatible.

`merge_and_unload()` prend un modèle PEFT chargé et retourne un modèle autonome dont les poids de l’adaptateur sont fusionnés aux poids de base. L’opération n’est pas effectuée sur place : il faut affecter sa valeur de retour puis utiliser le modèle retourné. La fusion peut supprimer le surcoût du chargement séparé de l’adaptateur, mais l’artefact fusionné ne permet plus aussi facilement de changer ou d’annuler cet adaptateur.

**Exemple.** Une équipe maintient deux adaptateurs pour le même modèle de base : l’un pour le support produit, l’autre pour la recherche interne de connaissances. Les conserver séparés permet de partager la même base et de publier chaque version indépendamment. Si la version de support approuvée doit fonctionner dans un environnement qui attend un seul artefact modèle, l’équipe peut produire et versionner une version fusionnée après avoir enregistré les éléments qui l’identifient.

Référence officielle : [documentation PEFT LoRA post-entraînement](https://huggingface.co/docs/peft/en/package_reference/lora).

question.en: A service uses one base model with several task-specific LoRA adapters and must switch among them during operation. Which artifact choice best preserves that flexibility?
question.fr: Un service utilise un modèle de base avec plusieurs adaptateurs LoRA propres à des tâches et doit passer de l’un à l’autre pendant son fonctionnement. Quel choix d’artefact préserve le mieux cette flexibilité ?

text.en: Keep each compatible adapter separate from the shared base model.
text.fr: Conserver chaque adaptateur compatible séparément du modèle de base partagé.

text.en: Merge all adapters into the base model with `merge_and_unload()` and discard their revisions.
text.fr: Fusionner tous les adaptateurs au modèle de base avec `merge_and_unload()` et supprimer leurs révisions.

text.en: Save only the final tokenizer because it identifies every adapter.
text.fr: Enregistrer uniquement le tokenizer final car il identifie chaque adaptateur.

text.en: Keep no record of the base-model revision so the adapter can load on any base.
text.fr: Ne garder aucune trace de la révision du modèle de base pour que l’adaptateur puisse se charger sur n’importe quelle base.

explanation.en: Separate adapters are designed for reuse with their compatible base and make adapter switching possible. `merge_and_unload()` creates a standalone merged model, which can simplify one fixed deployment but gives up that same swapping flexibility. Version records are essential for compatibility and traceability.
explanation.fr: Des adaptateurs séparés sont conçus pour être réutilisés avec leur base compatible et permettent de changer d’adaptateur. `merge_and_unload()` crée un modèle fusionné autonome, ce qui peut simplifier un déploiement fixe mais sacrifie cette flexibilité. Les informations de version sont indispensables à la compatibilité et à la traçabilité.

body.en:
After fine-tuning with PEFT, your adapter weights are a small delta on top of the frozen base model. Saving them with model.save_pretrained() writes only the adapter config and weights, typically a few hundred megabytes instead of tens of gigabytes. You can push directly to the Hub with push_to_hub().

When you need a self-contained model—for inference servers that do not support PEFT, or for export to ONNX or GGUF—you merge the adapter back into the base weights using merge_and_unload(). This call folds the low-rank matrices into the original weight tensors, returning a standard HuggingFace model with no adapter overhead. Always save the merged model separately; the original base model and adapter should be retained for reproducibility. Quantized adapters (QLoRA) must be dequantized before merging to avoid precision loss in the fused weights.

• **PEFT adapter checkpoint**: A lightweight directory containing adapter_config.json and adapter weights, loadable on top of any compatible base model.
• **merge_and_unload()**: PEFT method that permanently folds adapter parameters into the base model weights, producing a dependency-free HuggingFace model.
• **QLoRA dequantization**: The process of converting 4-bit quantized base weights back to full precision before merging to preserve numerical accuracy.
• **Hub versioning**: Using repository commits and tags on Hugging Face Hub to track adapter versions alongside their corresponding base model revision hashes.

question.en: What is the primary advantage of saving only the PEFT adapter rather than the full fine-tuned model?

text.en: The adapter runs faster at inference time without the base model
The adapter files are far smaller because they store only the delta weights, not the full model parameters
Adapters are automatically converted to ONNX format during saving
Saving an adapter removes the need to track the base model version

explanation.en: PEFT adapters store only the low-rank delta matrices added during fine-tuning, which are orders of magnitude smaller than the full base model weights, making storage and distribution much more efficient.

question.en: Which PEFT method call produces a standalone HuggingFace model with no remaining adapter dependency?

text.en: model.save_pretrained()
model.push_to_hub()
model.merge_and_unload()
model.disable_adapter_layers()

explanation.en: merge_and_unload() folds the adapter's low-rank matrices directly into the base model weight tensors, returning a standard model that can be used without the PEFT library.

question.en: Why must QLoRA adapters be dequantized before merging into the base model?

text.en: The Hugging Face Hub does not accept quantized model files
Dequantization is required to enable push_to_hub functionality
Merging quantized weights directly would introduce precision errors into the fused weight tensors
QLoRA adapters cannot be saved without dequantization

explanation.en: When base model weights are stored in 4-bit precision, merging adapter matrices without dequantizing first causes significant numerical precision loss in the resulting fused weights, degrading model quality.

• Saving only the adapter checkpoint dramatically reduces storage and transfer costs while preserving the ability to reproduce the fine-tuned model from any compatible base revision.
• merge_and_unload() is the standard path to a portable, self-contained model ready for ONNX export, quantization pipelines, or deployment to servers that do not support the PEFT library.
• Always record the exact base model name and revision hash alongside your adapter so that merging or inference can be reliably reproduced months later.

title.fr: Documentation des model cards et dataset cards

body.en: A model card is the README.md published with a model repository, with YAML metadata and human-readable documentation of intended uses, limitations, training information, datasets, and evaluation results. A dataset card is the README.md for a dataset repository; it documents the data’s content, use context, license, and relevant considerations such as biases. The two documents are complementary.
body.fr: Une model card est le README.md publié avec un dépôt de modèle, avec des métadonnées YAML et une documentation lisible sur les usages prévus, les limites, l’entraînement, les jeux de données et les évaluations. Une dataset card est le README.md d’un dépôt de données ; elle documente le contenu des données, leur contexte d’usage, leur licence et des considérations pertinentes telles que les biais. Ces deux documents sont complémentaires.

body.en:
## Objective

Document a fine-tuned model and its data so that another practitioner can determine fitness for purpose without inferring missing facts. On the Hugging Face Hub, the `README.md` of a model repository renders as a model card; the `README.md` of a dataset repository renders as a dataset card. Both can start with YAML metadata, but they document different artifacts.

## Model card: the model and its evidence

A model card should identify what the model does, its intended uses and limitations, the training parameters or experimental information, the datasets used for training, and evaluation results. YAML metadata may contain fields such as `language`, `license`, `datasets`, and `base_model`. For a fine-tune or adapter, `base_model` makes the lineage inspectable instead of leaving a user to guess which base weights are compatible.

## Dataset card: the data and its context

A dataset card should explain the data’s contents and context for use. Include enough information to inspect provenance or collection context, license, and material limitations or potential biases. Its metadata can make attributes such as language, license, size, and task categories discoverable. A dataset card does not prove that a derived model is suitable; it supplies the data context that a model card must reference.

**Example.** For a hypothetical adapter trained for support classification, the model card would identify the compatible base model, the intended classification use, limitations, and the evaluation method. The dataset card would describe the source, preparation, license, and known limits of the support examples. Do not insert benchmark results that were not actually measured.

Official references: [Model Cards](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/model-cards) and [Dataset Cards](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/datasets-cards).
body.fr:
## Objectif

Documentez un modèle fine-tuné et ses données afin qu’un autre praticien puisse évaluer son adéquation à l’usage sans devoir deviner les faits manquants. Sur le Hugging Face Hub, le `README.md` d’un dépôt de modèle est rendu comme model card ; le `README.md` d’un dépôt de données est rendu comme dataset card. Les deux peuvent commencer par des métadonnées YAML, mais ils documentent des artefacts différents.

## Model card : le modèle et ses éléments de preuve

Une model card doit indiquer ce que fait le modèle, ses usages prévus et ses limites, les paramètres d’entraînement ou informations expérimentales, les jeux de données utilisés et les résultats d’évaluation. Des métadonnées YAML peuvent contenir notamment `language`, `license`, `datasets` et `base_model`. Pour un fine-tune ou un adaptateur, `base_model` rend la filiation vérifiable : l’utilisateur n’a pas à deviner quels poids de base sont compatibles.

## Dataset card : les données et leur contexte

Une dataset card doit expliquer le contenu des données et leur contexte d’usage. Elle doit permettre d’examiner la provenance ou le contexte de collecte, la licence et les limites ou biais potentiels importants. Ses métadonnées peuvent rendre découvrables des attributs tels que la langue, la licence, la taille et les catégories de tâches. Une dataset card ne prouve pas qu’un modèle dérivé convient à un usage : elle fournit le contexte des données auquel la model card doit faire référence.

**Exemple.** Pour un adaptateur hypothétique entraîné à la classification de demandes de support, la model card indiquerait le modèle de base compatible, l’usage de classification prévu, les limites et la méthode d’évaluation. La dataset card décrirait la source, la préparation, la licence et les limites connues des exemples de support. N’ajoutez jamais des résultats de benchmark qui n’ont pas été réellement mesurés.

Références officielles : [Model Cards](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/model-cards) et [Dataset Cards](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/datasets-cards).

• **Model card YAML front matter**: Machine-readable metadata block at the top of README.md that populates Hub search filters for language, license, task type, datasets used, and evaluation metrics.
• **Intended use vs. out-of-scope use**: Explicitly documenting what the model is designed for and what it should not be used for reduces misuse and provides a baseline for governance audits.
• **Dataset card provenance section**: Records original data sources, collection dates, filtering criteria, and any third-party licenses so downstream users can assess legal and ethical compliance.
• **Carbon footprint reporting**: Including compute hours, hardware type, and region-based carbon intensity in training details supports reproducibility and environmental accountability.

In this lesson you will learn:
• The main serving frameworks for open-source LLMs including vLLM, TGI, and Ollama
• How continuous batching and PagedAttention improve GPU utilization during inference
• How to optimize a fine-tuned model for serving using quantization and compiled kernels
• Deployment options ranging from local endpoints to cloud-managed inference services

In this lesson you will learn:
• The main serving frameworks for open-source LLMs including vLLM, TGI, and Ollama
• How continuous batching and PagedAttention improve GPU utilization during inference
• How to optimize a fine-tuned model for serving using quantization and compiled kernels
• Deployment options ranging from local endpoints to cloud-managed inference services

Deploying a fine-tuned LLM for production requires more than loading the model and calling generate(). Serving frameworks handle batching, memory management, and API compatibility so your model can serve many concurrent users efficiently.

vLLM implements PagedAttention, which manages the KV-cache in non-contiguous memory blocks analogous to virtual memory paging, dramatically increasing throughput by eliminating memory waste. Text Generation Inference (TGI) from Hugging Face offers continuous batching, token streaming, and an OpenAI-compatible REST API, making it a drop-in backend for existing toolchains. Ollama targets local and edge deployment with a simple CLI and automatic GGUF quantization. For cloud deployment, options include Hugging Face Inference Endpoints, AWS SageMaker, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Azure ML managed endpoints. Quantizing the merged model to 4-bit or 8-bit with bitsandbytes or AWQ before serving reduces VRAM requirements without significant quality loss, enabling deployment on smaller GPU instances.

• **PagedAttention**: A memory management algorithm used by vLLM that stores KV-cache in fixed-size blocks, reducing memory fragmentation and enabling higher batch sizes at the same VRAM budget.
• **Continuous batching**: A scheduling strategy where new requests join the active compute batch as soon as sequence slots free up, maximizing GPU utilization compared to static batching.
• **OpenAI-compatible API**: TGI and vLLM expose /v1/chat/completions and /v1/completions endpoints, allowing any application built for OpenAI's API to switch to a self-hosted model with no code changes.
• **Inference quantization**: Post-training quantization methods such as AWQ or GPTQ compress model weights to 4-bit integers, reducing VRAM and memory bandwidth requirements while preserving most of the model's accuracy.

question.en: What problem does PagedAttention primarily solve in LLM serving?

text.en: It reduces the number of transformer layers needed for inference
It eliminates KV-cache memory fragmentation, allowing more requests to be batched on the same GPU
It compresses model weights to 4-bit precision automatically
It converts the model to ONNX format for faster CPU inference

explanation.en: PagedAttention manages KV-cache memory in fixed-size non-contiguous blocks, similar to OS virtual memory paging, which eliminates wasted reserved memory and allows vLLM to serve significantly more concurrent requests on the same hardware.

question.en: Which serving framework is best suited for local and edge deployment with automatic GGUF quantization support?

text.en: vLLM
Text Generation Inference (TGI)
Ollama
Triton Inference Server

explanation.en: Ollama is specifically designed for local and edge deployment, providing a simple CLI interface and automatically converting models to GGUF format for efficient CPU and GPU inference on consumer hardware.

question.en: What is the key advantage of continuous batching over static batching in an LLM inference server?

text.en: Continuous batching stores model weights in CPU RAM to free GPU memory
New requests are inserted into the active batch as sequence slots free up, maximizing GPU utilization
Continuous batching automatically quantizes each request to reduce compute
It processes each request sequentially to guarantee response order

explanation.en: In continuous batching, completed sequences immediately free their slot so waiting requests can join the batch without waiting for the entire batch to finish, which keeps GPU compute utilization much higher than static batching.

• vLLM's PagedAttention and continuous batching are the current state of the art for high-throughput GPU serving, delivering significantly more requests per second than naive inference loops.
• TGI's OpenAI-compatible API allows fine-tuned open-source models to slot directly into existing application stacks with minimal integration work.
• Applying post-training quantization (AWQ, GPTQ) before deployment can reduce VRAM requirements by up to 75%, making it economically viable to serve large models on smaller, cheaper GPU instances.

You now understand the leading serving frameworks, the memory and batching optimizations that make production LLM deployment practical, and the deployment options available across cloud and local environments.

In the final lesson, you will learn how to manage the cost, governance, and full lifecycle of your deployed fine-tuned models.

body.en:
In this lesson you will learn:
• How to estimate and monitor the total cost of fine-tuning and serving open-source LLMs
• Key governance frameworks and checklists for responsible deployment of fine-tuned models
• How to version, retire, and replace models as part of a structured MLOps lifecycle
• Strategies for monitoring model performance drift and triggering retraining pipelines

In this lesson you will learn:
• How to estimate and monitor the total cost of fine-tuning and serving open-source LLMs
• Key governance frameworks and checklists for responsible deployment of fine-tuned models
• How to version, retire, and replace models as part of a structured MLOps lifecycle
• Strategies for monitoring model performance drift and triggering retraining pipelines

Managing a fine-tuned LLM in production involves ongoing cost control, governance accountability, and a disciplined lifecycle process. Fine-tuning costs are dominated by GPU compute: track hours, instance type, and cloud region using experiment tracking tags so each adapter checkpoint has an associated cost record. Serving costs scale with tokens per second and concurrency; use autoscaling and spot or preemptible instances where latency SLAs allow.

Governance requires maintaining an audit trail from training data through deployment, including data licenses, bias evaluations, and sign-off records. Implement role-based access controls on model repositories and restrict who can promote a model to production. Define a lifecycle policy: models enter staging after evaluation, graduate to production after approval, and are deprecated with a sunset date when a better version is ready. Monitor production traffic for distribution shift using embedding-space drift detectors or output quality proxies, and feed alerts into automated retraining triggers. Versioning adapters and merged checkpoints with semantic version tags makes rollback straightforward when regressions are detected.

• **Total cost of ownership (TCO)**: The sum of fine-tuning compute, storage for checkpoints and datasets, serving infrastructure, and human engineering time—all of which must be tracked per model version to justify continued investment.
• **Model governance audit trail**: A documented chain of custody from raw training data (with licenses and consent records) through preprocessing, training runs, evaluations, and deployment approvals.
• **Staging → Production promotion gate**: A formal checkpoint where evaluation metrics, bias audits, and stakeholder sign-offs must all pass before a model version is exposed to production traffic.
• **Distribution shift monitoring**: Continuously comparing the statistical properties of live inputs or model outputs against a reference baseline to detect when the model is operating outside its validated distribution.

question.en: Which serving cost optimization strategy is most appropriate when a workload can tolerate occasional interruptions and has no strict latency SLA?

text.en: Using on-demand dedicated GPU instances reserved for three years
Running inference exclusively on CPU to avoid GPU costs entirely
Deploying on spot or preemptible GPU instances to reduce cost significantly
Disabling continuous batching to reduce power consumption

explanation.en: Spot or preemptible instances are offered by cloud providers at 60-90% discounts in exchange for the possibility of interruption. Batch or async workloads with flexible SLAs are ideal candidates, making this a common cost optimization for LLM serving.

question.en: What is the purpose of a staging-to-production promotion gate in a model lifecycle policy?

text.en: It automatically compresses the model weights before deployment to production
It ensures evaluation metrics, bias audits, and stakeholder approvals are all satisfied before live traffic exposure
It converts the model to ONNX format to meet production performance requirements
It merges all pending adapter checkpoints into a single release candidate

explanation.en: A promotion gate is a formal review step that requires quantitative evaluation benchmarks, bias and safety assessments, and human sign-offs to all pass before a model version is deployed to production, reducing the risk of regressions or harmful outputs reaching users.

question.en: Which technique is used to detect when a deployed model is receiving inputs that differ significantly from its training distribution?

text.en: Adapter merging
Continuous batching
Distribution shift monitoring using embedding-space drift detectors
YAML front matter validation

explanation.en: Distribution shift monitoring compares statistical properties of live inputs or outputs—often using embedding-space distance metrics or output quality proxies—against a reference baseline to detect when the model is being asked to handle data outside its validated distribution, signaling a need for retraining.

body.en:
• Tracking TCO per model version—including compute, storage, and engineering time—enables data-driven decisions about whether to retrain, replace, or retire a model and justifies infrastructure investments.
• A rigorous governance audit trail from data provenance through deployment approval is increasingly required by AI regulations and enterprise risk policies, and must be built into the workflow from the start.
• Distribution shift monitoring with automated retraining triggers closes the production feedback loop, ensuring that a fine-tuned model's quality is maintained as the real-world data it processes evolves over time.

## Module complete

You have completed the explanatory material in **Cost, Governance and Lifecycle Management**, the final lesson of the Packaging and Deployment course. You can now distinguish cost-efficient serving choices from governance controls, describe the audit trail that links data, training, evaluation, and deployment approval, and recognize why distribution shift monitoring belongs in the production lifecycle.

## Closing case

Consider a candidate adapter that is ready for a production review. Before promotion, its record should let reviewers identify the exact base model and adapter version, the applicable license and intended use, the evaluation evidence, known limitations, and the approval decision. If live inputs later differ materially from the validated setting, the team should investigate the change rather than treating the original evaluation as permanently sufficient.

This course does not include a hands-on lab, publication task, benchmark upload, or certification step. The completion point is the knowledge and decision framework explained in the course.
body.fr:
## Module terminé

Vous avez terminé le contenu explicatif de **Cost, Governance and Lifecycle Management**, la dernière leçon du cours Packaging and Deployment. Vous savez désormais distinguer les choix de serving efficients des contrôles de gouvernance, décrire la piste d’audit qui relie données, entraînement, évaluation et approbation de déploiement, et expliquer pourquoi la surveillance de dérive de distribution appartient au cycle de vie de production.

## Cas de clôture

Considérez un adaptateur candidat à une revue de production. Avant sa promotion, son dossier doit permettre aux évaluateurs d’identifier la version exacte du modèle de base et de l’adaptateur, la licence applicable et l’usage prévu, les éléments d’évaluation, les limites connues et la décision d’approbation. Si les entrées réelles diffèrent ensuite de manière significative du contexte validé, l’équipe doit examiner ce changement plutôt que de considérer l’évaluation initiale comme suffisante à jamais.

Cette formation ne contient pas de lab pratique, de tâche de publication, d’envoi de benchmark ni d’étape de certification. Le point de clôture est le cadre de connaissances et de décision expliqué dans le cours.

question.en: During a production review for a fine-tuned adapter, which record most directly supports a responsible promotion decision?
question.fr: Lors d’une revue de production d’un adaptateur fine-tuné, quel dossier appuie le plus directement une décision de promotion responsable ?

text.en: Only the current serving cost, because governance records can be recreated later.
text.fr: Uniquement le coût de serving actuel, car les éléments de gouvernance peuvent être recréés plus tard.

text.en: The base-model and adapter versions, applicable license and intended use, evaluation evidence, known limitations, and approval decision.
text.fr: Les versions du modèle de base et de l’adaptateur, la licence applicable et l’usage prévu, les éléments d’évaluation, les limites connues et la décision d’approbation.

text.en: A promise to publish results in a lab that is not part of the course.
text.fr: La promesse de publier des résultats dans un lab qui ne fait pas partie de la formation.

text.en: Only the family name of the underlying model.
text.fr: Uniquement le nom de la famille du modèle sous-jacent.

explanation.en: A promotion decision requires traceability across the artifact, its permitted and intended use, and the evidence for the deployment. Cost is one operational input, but it cannot replace lineage, evaluation, limitations, and accountable approval.
explanation.fr: Une décision de promotion exige une traçabilité de l’artefact, de son usage permis et prévu, ainsi que des éléments qui justifient le déploiement. Le coût est une donnée opérationnelle, mais il ne remplace pas la filiation, l’évaluation, les limites et une approbation responsable.
